S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 No. 2100 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. M.C. Upadhyaya, Advocate, for the applicants.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Deputy A.G., for the State of Uttarakhand.

The argument of the learned counsel for the applicants, while putting a challenge to the proceedings of Criminal Case No. 1028 of 2023, State Vs. Ramlal and others, whereby, the applicants have been summoned to be tried for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the IPC, is from two perspectives, that the applicants would draw an immunity from being prosecuted in view of the provisions contained under Section 334 of the U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act.

In answer to it, the issue should not be confused with the provisions of Land Revenue Act, and the U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act, which are two independent Acts, which function in an independent direction of law.

The provisions contained under Section 334 of the Z.A. & L.R. Act, cannot be borrowed to be applied in a prosecution dawn, because of the action taken under any of the provisions of the Land Revenue Act.
Thus, this argument extended by the learned counsel for the applicants is not acceptable by this Court.

Secondly, the learned counsel for the applicants has argued, that the entire prosecution would be bad in the eyes of law, because of non compliance of the provisions contained under Section 197 of the Cr.P.C., in an absence of there being any prior permission to prosecute a public servant.
It is an admitted case of the applicants, that applicant No.1 has already superannuated.
As such, on account of superannuation, he is no more a government servant, and as such, the implications of Section 197 of the Cr.P.C., will not apply to applicant No.1.

1

The applicant No.2 is still in service, and there is nothing on record to show, that prior to drawing the proceedings against the applicant No.2, there has been any compliance of the provisions contained under Section 197.
The learned Government Advocate, may file counter affidavit.
Let notices be issued to respondent No.2.
Steps to serve respondent No.2 would be taken by the applicant within a period of one week from today.
List this C-482 Application as soon as counter affidavit is filed.
Till the next date of listing, the summoning order as issued in Criminal Case No. 1028 of 2023, State Vs. Ramlal and others, would be kept in abeyance, qua the applicant No.2 only.

(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) Dated 19.10.2023 Shiv State vs Unknown on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163812696/
